chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: Hal Stanley's clubs: Rum Boogie, Downbeat and the Cotton Club
summary: Lee and Willard list the clubs Kay Starr's husband Hal Stanley ran, including a Hollywood Cotton Club that opened with Basie in February 1949.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You were mentioning off the tape yesterday, that you knew Kay Starr and was it? From recording, and you introduced her to Hal Stanley, whom she married, and Hal Stanley, you were telling me all the different clubs that Hal Stanley operated. What were they?
Yeah. Hal Stanley operated the Rum
Boogie, up on Highland Blvd., that's where C.P. Johnson was, and I still think that at one time they had another club there that he called the Onyx Club.
Before the Rum Boogie?
Well, I think it was after.
After.

And then he opened the Downbeat on Central Avenue, which was across the street, you know, from the last one last word and down the street from the Club Alabam. And then the other club that he opened was where the old Florentine Gardens was on Hollywood Blvd.
And he called it the Cotton Club?
He called it the Cotton Club. And it closed, you know, but he was a Basie lover and a blues lover, and so he opened with Basie and Pearl Bailey.
And that was -- they were working opposite the Hollywood Empire, which was down the street and around he corner from Vine Street where Duke Ellington was.
That's right.
And so Duke and Basie were like, 4 blocks from each other.
Right. Right.
In February of '49.
That sounds right. That was '49, huh?
Yeah, 'cause I was working at the

Gene
Empire for Jay Norman.
I see. Well, then we got those dates straight. Well then, yes .. now,
She was already married to Hal Stanley by then, wasn't she?
Uh huh, yeah. Yes, she was married to him.
Uh huh.
